name: Alverine

overview.mechanism: A smooth-muscle relaxant studied for irritable bowel syndrome symptoms; this role does not establish clinical efficacy for every formulation [[ALV-RCT,ALV-LIVER]].
uses: Symptomatic IBS treatment has been studied with single-agent alverine citrate. Alverine–simethicone is a separate combination product; its evidence must not be attributed to alverine alone [[ALV-RCT]].

evidence.title: Clinical evidence and limitations
evidence.intro: Study regimens are descriptions of research, not prescribing recommendations.

rows.design: Three-center, double-blind randomized placebo-controlled study; 107 patients; 12 weeks.
rows.intervention: Single-agent alverine citrate capsule formulation versus placebo.
rows.findings: Pain-severity and pain-frequency improvement did not differ significantly from placebo; the larger mean reduction in the alverine arm was also nonsignificant.
rows.limitations: Studied capsule differs from the local Profenil tablet. High placebo response; no evidence here of disease modification, long-term benefit or equivalence to alverine–simethicone.

rows.intervention: Alverine citrate exposure in an older adult.
rows.findings: Jaundice and abdominal discomfort developed after exposure; alternative hepatitis causes were excluded and liver tests normalized after withdrawal.
rows.limitations: Suspected drug-induced liver injury from a case report: supports a safety signal, not an incidence estimate or a predictable dose–toxicity relationship.

sources.citation: Alverine citrate fails to relieve the symptoms of irritable bowel syndrome: results of a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial. PubMed PMID: 12030962.
A case report of alverine-citrate-induced acute hepatitis. PubMed PMID: 20375645.

serious: Suspected acute hepatitis with jaundice has been reported after alverine exposure, improving after discontinuation. Rare reports cannot determine frequency [[ALV-LIVER]].

renal: The cited IBS trial does not establish CKD adjustment or dialysis use; no renal regimen is inferred from antispasmodic activity [[ALV-RCT]].
